description: Team CropSave is a group of 5 students and developers from Pakistan building a drought prediction tool for farmers. We use NASA satellite data to give farmers a simple 30-day drought risk forecast so they can protect their crops before it is too late. Our team has skills in Full Stack Development, Machine Learning, AI Engineering, and Data Science.
summary:
CropSave is a web application that helps farmers in 
Pakistan make smarter decisions by combining NASA 
satellite data with AI-powered crop yield prediction. 

The app has two modules working together. The first 
module uses NASA POWER API to predict drought risk 
for the next 30 days for any district in Pakistan, 
showing farmers a clear LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH risk 
level with simple farming advice. The second module 
uses a machine learning model trained on 480 real 
agricultural plots across Pakistan to predict cotton 
fiber yield, with SHAP explainability showing farmers 
why the prediction was made.

Together, these modules give Pakistani farmers one 
complete answer: is drought coming, and how will it 
affect my crop yield? This helps farmers decide when 
to plant, how to manage water, and what to expect 
from their harvest.

NASA data used: NASA POWER API for real-time climate 
data including soil moisture, rainfall, temperature, 
and humidity. The app is live and accessible on any 
mobile phone.
details:
CropSave is an AI-powered drought prediction web application built for Pakistani farmers. The app uses real NASA satellite data to predict drought risk for the next 30 days for any district in Pakistan.

How it works: A farmer opens the app on their phone, selects their district from an interactive Pakistan map, and within seconds receives a drought risk level of LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH. The app also provides simple farming advice on what action to take based on the risk level.

NASA Data Used: We use the NASA POWER API to fetch real-time soil moisture, rainfall, temperature, and humidity data for any GPS location in Pakistan. We also use NASA SMAP soil moisture satellite data and NASA TRMM/GPM historical precipitation data.

Technology Stack: The backend is built with Python and FastAPI, deployed on Render.com. The frontend is built with React.js and Tailwind CSS, with Leaflet.js for interactive maps and Chart.js for data visualization. The machine learning model is a Random Forest Classifier built with Scikit-learn, trained on 10 years of NASA climate data for 20 Pakistan districts. The model outputs a drought risk score from 0 to 100, converted to LOW, MEDIUM, or HIGH risk levels.

Impact: Pakistan has over 60 million farmers who lose billions of rupees in crops every year due to drought. CropSave makes NASA satellite intelligence accessible to every farmer through a simple mobile-friendly interface, helping them make better decisions about planting, water usage, and crop management before it is too late.

Live App: https://cropsave.vercel.app

GitHub: https://github.com/ammarzia124/Crop-Save
